clue.text: God of war sending master of weaponry to the front

indicators.note: sending something to the front means lifting it out of its place before moving it forward

parts.note: arms are weapons collectively
M is a standard abbreviation for master; it is the M already inside the weapons word

explanation.surface: A war god dispatches his chief armourer to lead the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: The M of ARMS is moved from third place to the front, giving MARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars is the Roman deity of warfare, so he is literally a god of war.

clue.text: A rocky romance fuelled by one drink

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: being fuelled by something means taking it in, so one more letter goes inside
a rocky relationship is unstable, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An unsteady love affair kept going by alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' looks like part of the story of a boozy romance; here it is the definition, a coffee rather than anything alcoholic.
explanation.definitionFit: An americano is a coffee made by diluting espresso with hot water, a common café beverage.

clue.text: Second-rate accommodation

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
pace is a rate of movement

explanation.surface: Somebody complains that their lodgings are shabby and inferior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second-rate' reads as one hyphenated adjective but splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Space and accommodation both mean room available to hold people or things.

clue.text: Arctic city bordered by two rivers

indicators.note: something bordered by others has them on either side, so it sits between them

parts.note: PO, the Italian river, and R, the abbreviation for river
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A northern settlement hemmed in by a pair of waterways.
explanation.walkthrough: The two rivers go on opposite sides of the city: PO before, R after.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar describes the regions around the poles, and the Arctic is the northern one.

clue.text: Liberal sort of supports local produce

indicators.note: in a down entry whatever supports another piece sits beneath it, so it comes after

parts.note: a local is a British term for one's neighbourhood pub
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
-ish means sort of, as in 'greenish'

explanation.surface: A tolerant type is keen on buying food grown nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: L and ISH sit under the pub in the down entry. 'Produce' looks like the noun for farm goods; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To publish a book or paper is to produce it and issue it to the public.

clue.text: Fruit tree died covered in sticky stuff

parts.note: the lime is a citrus fruit tree
D is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A citrus tree perished after being smothered in gummy residue.
explanation.walkthrough: Birdlime is a sticky substance once smeared on branches to trap birds; to lime a twig is to coat it so.
explanation.definitionFit: Limed can mean smeared with birdlime, the gluey paste used for catching small birds.

clue.text: Pest controller putting some bitumen all over

indicators.note: something turned all over is flipped end to end, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: part means some of a thing
tar is a bitumen

explanation.surface: An exterminator spreads tarry stuff everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pest controller' sounds like a person, but the device that catches vermin counts too.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat trap controls pests by catching rodents, so it is a mechanical pest controller.

clue.text: Dirty priest pulled from wreck

indicators.note: pulling something from a word takes it out, leaving the rest

parts.note: to spoil is to wreck
P is the abbreviation for priest

explanation.surface: A grubby cleric is dragged out of a crashed vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty' looks like an adjective for the priest, but it is a verb meaning to make unclean.
explanation.definitionFit: To soil something is to make it unclean, the verb sense of making something grubby.

clue.text: Mum noisily prepares breakfast?

indicators.note: doing something noisily means it is heard, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: mum! is a call for silence, like shh
to ready something is to prepare it

explanation.surface: Mother clatters about in the kitchen getting the morning meal ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like Mother but means keep quiet. Shreddies is a British breakfast cereal of shredded wheat squares.
explanation.definitionFit: Shreddies is a brand of wholegrain cereal eaten in the morning, so it serves as a breakfast.

clue.text: Independent setter interrupted by a good idea

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for independent

indicators.note: a word that is interrupted is broken open so that something else comes in mid-way

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as me
A as written, plus G for good

explanation.surface: The Independent's compiler is cut off mid-flow by a bright thought.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is the clue writer, so ME; it is broken open to take AG.
explanation.definitionFit: An image can be a mental picture or conception, much like an idea held in the mind.

clue.text: Where should I drop off barrels full of gold paint?

parts.note: a bed is where one drops off to sleep
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
B is an abbreviation for barrel

explanation.surface: A worker asks where to unload casks of gold-coloured paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop off' reads as delivering the barrels but means falling asleep; the gold is loaded ahead of a single barrel's B. 'Paint' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedaub is to smear or daub crudely with paint or something messy.

clue.text: Miles above the ground collecting temperature data

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for miles

indicators.note: collecting something means gathering it in, so it ends up inside

parts.note: aerial means in the air, above the ground
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A weather balloon miles high gathers readings of how hot it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Data' looks like the thing being collected in the story, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Material can mean information or facts gathered for use, as in research material.

clue.text: Special red wine I'd drunk making one legless

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for special

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about, so these letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Knocking back a special red has left someone legless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legless' is British slang for very drunk, which fits the wine; here it literally means without legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidewinder is a desert rattlesnake that moves sideways, and snakes have no legs at all.

clue.text: Rich duke assuming king's role in castle

indicators.note: taking on someone's role means standing in their place, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A wealthy nobleman takes the monarch's place in a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: K for king in KEEP is swapped out for D.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep and rich both describe a full, intense colour or a resonant low voice.

clue.text: Float boat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to start a company or offer it on the market

explanation.walkthrough: Both words seem nautical, but 'Float' is the business sense of starting up a venture.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch a firm is to set it going, and a launch is also a kind of motor-powered vessel.

clue.text: Fell runner occasionally stopped around entrance to valley

parts.note: a nose runs now and then, during a cold

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: an engine that died has stopped

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is where you go in, its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of valley

explanation.surface: A fell runner who keeps halting near the mouth of a dale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell runner' suggests a hill racer; 'Fell' is the definition, past tense of fall, and 'runner occasionally' is a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: To nosedive is to plunge sharply downward, so nosedived means fell steeply.

clue.text: Trump is making a comeback with something seedy?

parts.note: to cap something is to outdo or trump it

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the word travels back the way it came

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round
cum is Latin for with, as in 'kitchen-cum-diner'

explanation.surface: A political figure staging a return alongside something disreputable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' and 'seedy' suggest politics and sleaze; the pepper is seedy simply because it is full of seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A capsicum is a pepper whose hollow centre is packed with seeds, so it is literally seedy.

clue.text: Pet rabbit husband's neglected

indicators.note: something neglected is left out, so it drops away

parts.note: to rabbit is British slang for chatter on
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: The family bunny is ignored by the man of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet rabbit' reads as one animal, but rabbit means talk, as in 'rabbit on'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat is one of the commonest domestic animals kept as a companion.

clue.text: Ultimately erratic in nature, subject to change

definitions.text: Ultimately erratic in nature, subject to change

indicators.note: letters subject to change may be altered in order
ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of erratic
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something whose character is unpredictable and liable to shift.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: something erratic by nature and liable to change is unsure.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncertain means not fixed or settled, so something unpredictable and liable to alter fits.

clue.text: C note ignored by player

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so it drops from the word

parts.note: a contestant is a player in a game
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A musician passes over the note C.
explanation.walkthrough: 'C note' looks like a musical note or a hundred-dollar bill; C is the definition, the physical constant for the speed of light.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics c is the speed of light, a fixed value, so it is a constant.

clue.text: Review articles discussed works of fiction

parts.note: the indefinite articles an and a

indicators.note: something discussed is spoken about, so it is judged by its sound

parts.note: lies are invented stories

explanation.surface: A critic's review discusses some pieces of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works of fiction' suggests novels; here it means untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: To analyse something is to examine it closely, which is what a review does.

clue.text: Dry boards chip and split

indicators.note: to board is to get on or into, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a chip is a small bit
sec is a word for dry wine

explanation.surface: Dried-out planks chip and crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boards' looks like the wooden planks, but it is a verb, meaning gets on board.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut into two parts, so to split down the middle.

clue.text: Bats best in a helmet

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, so the letters go haywire

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricketer bats best when wearing a helmet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' looks like a verb or flying animals; it is the adjective meaning mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A basinet is a light, close-fitting medieval steel headpiece worn as armour.

clue.text: Put to work, some decades until going into retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the letters run in reverse
some means only part of the words is taken

parts.note: the letters running across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone worked for decades before finally retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a career; read decaDES Until backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Used is the past tense of use, meaning put into service or employed for a task.

clue.text: Kit used for exploration, primarily, in sea?

definitions.text: Kit used for exploration, primarily, in sea

parts.note: surface reading: equipment taken on an expedition
setter's reading: gear for diving underwater, whose name is itself built from initial letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'Primarily' hints that the answer is an acronym: Self-Contained Underwater Breathing Apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: Scuba gear is the breathing equipment divers use to explore the sea floor.

clue.text: Mixed metaphors involving Earth's climate

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so a letter is added within
mixed things are jumbled together, so the letters change order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for Earth

explanation.surface: Jumbled figures of speech when writing about the planet's weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earth's climate' reads as one phrase; the apostrophe-s is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Atmosphere can mean the prevailing mood or climate of a place, as in a tense climate.

clue.text: Farmer getting components for combine

indicators.note: components are parts within a whole, so the letters lie inside the words

parts.note: the letters running across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A farmer buys spare parts for a combine harvester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combine' looks like the farm machine, but it is the verb meaning join.
explanation.definitionFit: To merge is to blend or join together into one, which is to combine.

clue.text: Wood cabin sheltering emotionless rangers?

indicators.note: something sheltering another holds it inside

parts.note: a hut is a small cabin

indicators.note: emotionless means without feelings, read as without the innards, so only the outside letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of rangers

explanation.surface: A forest hut gives shelter to stony-faced park rangers.
explanation.walkthrough: A hurst is an old word for a wooded hill or copse, familiar from English place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurst is an archaic term for a wood or wooded rise, surviving in names like Pinehurst.

clue.text: Inspector runs after aroused voyeurs

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other in the answer
aroused means stirred up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A police inspector chases a pair of excited peeping toms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs after' reads as chasing; 'after' is placing R behind the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A surveyor examines land or buildings professionally, an inspector of property.

clue.text: Wisdom, perhaps of old people?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... Wisdom, the British film comedian, is one example of this first name
second meaning: belonging to the medieval invaders from northern France

explanation.walkthrough: Norman Wisdom was a slapstick British comedy star of the 1950s; 'Wisdom' looks like old people's knowledge. Norman is also this puzzle's setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman is both a given name, as borne by the comedian, and an adjective for the Normans of 1066.

clue.text: Large area with national borders, essentially

definitions.text: Large area with national borders, essentially

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large
A is the abbreviation for area
N is the abbreviation for national

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, so only the middle letter is kept

parts.note: the central letter of borders

explanation.surface: Describes a big territory with frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer as well as building it: a big area with national borders is a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A land is a country or nation, a large territory marked out by frontiers.

clue.text: Coming over every so often to cheer her up

indicators.note: coming over suggests turning round, so the letters are read from the end
every so often means at intervals, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: Someone visits now and then to lift a friend's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheer her up' reads as one phrase, but 'up' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Erect means upright or standing straight, so it is a synonym of up.

clue.text: Take the Sun King's military vehicle

parts.note: to tan is to take the sun, to sunbathe
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Seize Louis XIV's armoured car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Sun King' looks like Louis XIV of France; the phrase splits into 'Take the Sun' and 'King'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tank is an armoured fighting vehicle on caterpillar tracks used by armies.
